title: Protocol for rapid obtention and fractionation of anaerobic bacterial conditioned media to study calcium signaling in enteroendocrine cells
protocol: Add 100 μL of the first inoculum of Akkermansia muciniphila in two flasks containing BHI medium.
Incubate the flasks with bacteria in an anaerobiosis chamber at 37°C for 42 hours until bacterial growth reaches OD600 = 0.6.
Keep two additional flasks containing only BHI under the same conditions as negative controls.
Check for contamination by mounting a slide and coverslip containing 10 μL of bacterial suspension or unconditioned media from both types of flasks.
Collect Akkermansia muciniphila conditioned medium (BHI CM) from the incubated flasks.
Prepare an ice bath.
Organize a biological safety cabinet to work in a sterile environment.
Adjust the setting of the 50 mL Falcon tube centrifuge to 5,000 g at 4°C and wait until the temperature cools down.
Transfer bacterial suspension into a sterile 50 mL Falcon tube and store in an ice bath.
Transfer pure BHI medium into another sterile 50 mL Falcon tube and store in an ice bath.
Position the tubes alternately in the centrifuge.
Centrifuge at 5,000 g, 4°C for 10 minutes.
Collect supernatant within a biological safety cabinet and transfer to a new sterile 50 mL Falcon tube.
Collect pure BHI medium in the same manner as supernatant collection.
Discard bacterial pellet.
Repeat centrifugation step if necessary to completely decant planktonic Akkermansia cells.
Inside a biological safety cabinet, transfer sterilely and individually the BHI CM or BHI to the centricon top.
Properly identify the centricon cover and body.
Keep the original tubes containing BHI CM and BHI in an ice bath during the entire procedure.
Place the centricons in the centrifuge so that the weight is balanced inside the centrifuge.
Centrifuge at 5,000 g, 4°C for 20 min.
Using a micropipette, make repeated flushes in the center of the centricon membrane to homogenize the fraction being concentrated.
Be careful not to touch the membrane with the tip to prevent tearing.
Repeat steps until BHI CM and BHI are concentrated to a 3 mL volume in the top of the centricon.
Transfer the <3 kDa fraction if it increases rapidly, ensuring it does not reach the membrane.
Keep transferred fractions on ice (4°C) in properly identified sterile Falcon tubes.
Do not mix >3 kDa and <3 kDa fractions or BHI CM with BHI.
Dispose used micropipette tips after each use.
Identify cap and body of the tubes and centricon used carefully.
Sterilize each fraction by transferring them to new sterile containers using a syringe attached to a 0.22 μm filter.
Aliquot and immediately store sterilized fractions at -80°C until needed.
Dilute the Ca2+ indicator, such as Fluo-4/AM, according to the manufacturer’s specifications.
Keep the diluted Ca2+ indicator in an ice bath.
Transfect cells with Ca2+ indicator plasmids if necessary.
Turn on the CO2 and heating of the confocal microscope stage by setting it to 37°C.
Adjust laser settings and parameters for live imaging.
Perform experiments using a Leica SP8 confocal microscope with a ×63 objective lens, 1.4 NA.
Excite at 488 nm and detect emission between 505-525 nm.
Use frame scanning module at 15 f/s during 5 min of imaging.
Add the fluorescent probe Fluo-4/AM to one of the wells of the STC-1 plate at the concentration indicated by the manufacturer.
Incubate the plate containing the probe in a 37°C incubator for 15–20 minutes.
Remove one glass coverslip from the 6-well plate and transfer it to an imaging chamber on a Leica SP8 Confocal System.
Perfuse the imaging chamber continuously with HEPES buffer solution.
Select an image field where the cells are spread out and the initial fluorescence emission is homogeneous.
Start live-image recording of the cell in its basal state for approximately 100 seconds.
Add the desired stimulus, such as BHI CM (>3 kDa) at 1% or 10% (v/v).
Continue recording the response for approximately another 300 seconds after adding the stimulus.
Save and properly name the obtained image file in a folder designated for confocal microscopy data.
Repeat steps from adding the probe to the well until saving the image, but this time use 10% BHI (>3 kDa) as the negative control.
